Find the area $A$ bounded by the polar curve $r=2+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

When $r(\theta )=2+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )$, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+{sin}^{2}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )}{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{9}{2}+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9}{2}\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )}{8}){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9\pi }{4}+4) \\  & =2+\frac{9\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
